quarterly_data.signal: CFO Charles Tsai: Q2 2026 consolidated revenue was TWD 23.28 billion, up 37% year-over-year and 12% sequentially. Gross profit TWD 7.15 billion, gross margin 30.73% (vs 28.77% in Q1); operating profit TWD 4.01 billion, operating margin 17% (vs 14.9% in Q1); net income attributable to shareholders TWD 2.98 billion, EPS TWD 15.28 - net income and EPS a new quarterly high. CFO: utilization improved and the operational issues that affected Q1 profitability began to normalize; the improvement was not simply a function of higher volume (manufacturing efficiency, material cost, productivity, opex efficiency).
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue TWD 23.28 billion (+37% YoY, +12% QoQ); GM 30.73% (Q1 28.77%); OPM 17% (Q1 14.9%); net income TWD 2.98 billion; EPS TWD 15.28

quarterly_data.signal: CFO on the second-half outlook: 'Looking into the second half, I think we remain constructive, but I would not suggest modeling gross margin as a straight line upward every quarter' - product transitions, customer deployment cycles, foreign exchange and business mix can all create quarter-to-quarter fluctuation; the company manages for a stable and reasonable margin while growing the earnings base. Higher-growth businesses are becoming larger and some more mature businesses are beginning to recover. CFO: remain constructive on AI infrastructure and capital equipment, and seeing improving conditions across all parts of the industrial portfolio. No numeric guidance given.

CFO on capital equipment (semiconductor equipment): BizLink's role has expanded from components toward higher-level assembly and system integration; this is translating into accelerating growth, with quarterly sales reaching a new level. 'Today, we have reasonable order visibility extending into the second half of 2027', and discussions with customers are already beginning to extend into 2028; the company is deepening engineering engagement and expanding subsystem capabilities. CFO: broader industrial businesses show a gradual recovery that is not uniform across end markets.
quarterly_data.figure: Order visibility into the second half of 2027; customer discussions extending into 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Felix Teng on optics: a structural extension of the data connectivity business; the opportunity is more than successive transitions from 800G to 1.6T - density is becoming increasingly important and optics move closer to the system level through optical circuit switching and MPO / CPO architectures, which 'may develop on different timelines'. Both greenfield and installed-base (hyperscale upgrade) opportunities; 'we see more and more demands and also inquiries about our ... optical solutions'. XFS gives BizLink an established position in fiber assemblies, harnesses and related optical connectivity solutions. CEO: 'almost every path toward larger and denser AI infrastructure requires more sophisticated optical connectivities'.

CEO: copper continues to play an important role where distance and system architecture allow, while optical connectivity becomes more important as bandwidth and transmission distances increase; 'We do not see this as a simple transition from copper to optics' - different architectures will need different combinations. BizLink participates across power, copper and optics. On rack power, the industry is evaluating multiple approaches including higher amperage and higher voltage; CEO expects multiple power architectures to operate at the same time, and BizLink's power capabilities span cables, busbars and increasingly higher-power solutions. In HPC the company has expanded from traditional connectivity into higher-speed data solutions and more sophisticated power solutions.

CEO on AI demand: AI infrastructure is shifting from securing compute to deploying it at scale; constraints can shift from compute to networking, to power, or to facilities and utilities, which can create variability in procurement and deployment schedules even when underlying requirements remain strong. CEO: 'investment cycle of this magnitude will include periods of acceleration and period of digestion'. CFO: today's AI generation already contributes to revenue and profit growth while engineering teams work with customers on future platforms, in some areas beyond the next generation into N+2 solutions.

CFO on capacity: the company will keep investing (engineering, technology, qualification, automation, NPI, capacity) but intends to keep capex discipline relative to the scale of the business, broadly consistent with historical capital intensity; 'We will not build capacity simply because demand expectation are high', may reallocate capacity from mature programs to faster-growing ones, and is 'willing to leave some business on the table' where economics do not justify the capital. Chairman Roger Liang: more competitors are spending across data connectivity, power and optics; BizLink does not compete on price for its own sake and builds on multiple generations of high-speed copper qualification, which helped it move into power and supports its optics development.
